review_notes: I read the whole file and the definitions it depends on: IGame.Fits in CombinatorialGames/Surreal/Basic.lean, and Fits.birthday_le and Fits.birthday_lt in NormalFormSupport.lean. The strongest duplication is the Fits-construction block shared by birthday_ofSets_le_of_mem and birthday_ofSets_lt_of_mem. The three-fold `hr : 0 < r` derivation is weaker, since it is only four lines, but it is identical each time. I did not check whether Mathlib already has a lemma for it. The Fits direction (`Fits z.out cut`) is inferred from how `apply IGame.Fits.birthday_le` is used in the proofs. The proposed helper statements are untested, and the elaboration details (instance arguments, `generalize_proofs`) may need small adjustments. round_add_of_eq and round_mul_of_eq share a structure, but they differ in their option sets and in the grind goals, so I did not report them.

findings.excerpt:
apply IGame.Fits.birthday_le
  constructor
  · intro x hx
    let := IGame.Numeric.of_mem_moves hx
    rw [IGame.Numeric.not_le]
findings.problem: Both theorems repeat the same 14-line argument that shows the cut on `out '' s | out '' t` fits `z.out`. In each, the left-move and right-move cases both run `of_mem_moves`, `Numeric.not_le`, `simp only [moves_ofSets, Player.cases]`, `obtain ⟨a, ha, rfl⟩`, then `mk_lt_mk` with `out_eq` and `hL`/`hR`. The two copies are character-for-character the same, apart from one extra indentation level in the second theorem. Within each copy the two cases are also near-duplicates of each other.
findings.proposed_change: Extract a lemma stating the Fits fact once. Take the same implicit arguments `{s t} {z} [Small s] [Small t] {H}` and hypotheses `hL hR` as the two theorems. Its statement would be `IGame.Fits z.out !{out '' s | out '' t}`, plus whatever Numeric instance the `generalize_proofs` step needs. Prove it with the current `constructor` block. Then the two theorems become `rw [ofSets_eq_mk, ← out_eq z]; exact IGame.Fits.birthday_le (fits_out_ofSets_of_mem hL hR)` and `... IGame.Fits.birthday_lt (fits_out_ofSets_of_mem hL hR) (by rwa [← mk_eq_mk, ← ofSets_eq_mk, out_eq, eq_comm])`. The two cases could be proved with a local `have key : ∀ {a b}, ...` or `all_goals`, but the shared lemma is the main fix.
findings.benefit: The set-to-representative reasoning appears once, so a change to `ofSets_eq_mk` or to the `Fits` API needs one edit instead of four near-identical edits. Each birthday theorem then reads as a direct application of `Fits.birthday_le` or `Fits.birthday_lt`.

findings.excerpt:
have hr : 0 < r := by
    rw [← neg_lt_self_iff]
    apply (add_lt_add_iff_left x).mp
    simpa only [sub_eq_add_neg] using h.1.trans h.2
findings.problem: Three theorems open with the same four-line proof that membership of some `y` in `Ioo (x - r) (x + r)` forces `0 < r`. The copies are at lines 157–160, 170–173 and 181–184, and the argument is nontrivial: it uses `neg_lt_self_iff`, `add_lt_add_iff_left` and `sub_eq_add_neg`.
findings.proposed_change: Add a private lemma `pos_of_mem_Ioo_sub_add {x y r : Surreal} (h : y ∈ Ioo (x - r) (x + r)) : 0 < r`. Its proof is the existing four lines. Then replace each of the three `have hr` blocks with `have hr := pos_of_mem_Ioo_sub_add h`. In `round_of_zero_mem` the call is made before `cases x`, and the call is the same as in the other two uses. This lemma would sit next to the private `sub_lt_add_of_pos`, which it complements as a converse.
findings.benefit: It removes twelve duplicated lines. It also names the fact that a nonempty rounding interval forces a positive radius, which the three theorems rely on, and it keeps the proof in one place.
